patches.find: Yo la oía con nueve años y la cantaba en el colegio.
patches.replace: Yo la oía con quince años y la cantaba en el instituto.
patches.why: Timeline: Fali is 58 (born c.1968); the tape is from 1984, when he was 15-16, not 9.

patches.find: I used to listen to it when I was nine and sing it at school.
patches.replace: I used to listen to it when I was fifteen and sing it at school.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: Esa noche bajé al trastero la caja de casetes y las fui
patches.replace: Esa noche bajé al trastero a por la caja de casetes y las fui
patches.why: Logic: the box was in the storeroom she was clearing in October ('vaciando un trastero'); she goes down for it, not takes it down.

patches.find: That night I took the box of cassettes down to the storeroom and listened
patches.replace: That night I went down to the storeroom for the box of cassettes and listened
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: —grabados de la radio con anuncios y todo—
patches.replace: —grabación de radio, con anuncios y todo—
patches.why: Agreement: 'grabados' has no masculine plural referent (agrupación/cinta); nominal apposition is clean.

patches.find: “And the judge’s children plagiarise.”
patches.replace: “And in the judge’s house, plagiarism.”
patches.why: EN: the twist is on 'casa' (en la de la jueza, plagio); 'children' adds a meaning the Spanish lacks.

patches.find: The theatre brought the house down.
patches.replace: The house came down.
patches.why: EN: 'the theatre brought the house down' is illogical (performers bring the house down).

patches.find: the formula needs the imperfect subjunctive.
patches.replace: the formula needs the past subjunctive (imperfect, or pluperfect for a completed action: ¡ni que hubiera visto un fantasma!).
patches.why: Accuracy: ni que + pluperfect subjunctive is standard; 'needs the imperfect' is too narrow.

patches.find: The formula ¡Ni que…! always takes the imperfect subjunctive: ni que fuera.
patches.replace: The formula ¡Ni que…! takes the past subjunctive, here the imperfect: ni que fuera.
patches.why: Accuracy: 'always the imperfect' is wrong (pluperfect subjunctive also used).

patches.find: ¿Qué se le ofrece a la señoría?
patches.replace: ¿Qué se le ofrece a su señoría?
patches.why: Fixed form of address is 'su señoría'.

patches.find: Que yo grabé ese ensayo el 2 de octubre, y hay vídeo.
patches.replace: Que ese ensayo lo colgó mi sobrino el 2 de octubre, y hay vídeo.
patches.why: Consistency with story: the nephew posted the video.

patches.find: I recorded that rehearsal on 2 October, and there’s a video.
patches.replace: My nephew posted that rehearsal on 2 October, and there’s a video.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: And the judge’s children plagiarise. I’m
patches.replace: And in the judge’s house, plagiarism. I’m
patches.why: EN matches the story fix (twist on 'casa', not children).

patches.find: ¿Tú por mi peña tres días antes de tu actuación?
patches.replace: ¿Tú por mi peña en plena semana de preliminares?
patches.why: Story: Reyes visits Fali the day before her performance, not three days before.

patches.find: You at my club three days before your performance?
patches.replace: You at my club in the middle of preliminaries week?
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: que llevaba doce días durmiendo mal
patches.replace: que llevaba tres noches durmiendo mal
patches.why: Timeline: the repair happens two or three days after he finds the crack (12 days is the time left to the Llamadas).

patches.find: who had been sleeping badly for twelve days
patches.replace: who had been sleeping badly for three nights
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: le robaban a su padre los palillos
patches.replace: le robaban a su padre los palos
patches.why: Candombe drums are played with a 'palo' (one stick + hand), not 'palillos' (needs Montevideo check).

patches.find: With a fronted direct object the pronoun is obligatory
patches.replace: With a fronted definite direct object used as a topic (not as a contrastive focus) the pronoun is obligatory
patches.why: Accuracy: focus-fronted objects (AQUEL TAMBOR había hecho) take no clitic.

patches.find: Pasá, pasá, que hace frío. ¿Vos sos amiga de la gurisa?
patches.replace: Pasá, pasá, sentate un rato. ¿Vos venís con la gurisa?
patches.why: Montevideo in Jan-Feb is midsummer ('hace frío' wrong); avoid assuming the learner's gender.

patches.find: Come in, come in, it’s cold. Are you a friend of the girl’s?
patches.replace: Come in, come in, sit down for a bit. Have you come with the girl?
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: ¿Me contás cómo era el Mediomundo
patches.replace: ¿Me cuenta cómo era el Mediomundo
patches.why: Learner otherwise addresses don Obdulio with usted (steps 2-3); keep consistent.

patches.find: Qué lindo tambor. ¿Y esa raja en la lonja?
patches.replace: Qué lindo tambor. ¿Su padre lo sacó del conventillo?
patches.why: Scene/step 2: the drum is already repaired, so a visible crack contradicts; new line also leads naturally to 'El tambor se lo llevó abrazado'.

patches.find: What a beautiful drum. And that crack in the head?
patches.replace: What a beautiful drum. Did your father get it out of the tenement?
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: Pasá, que hace frío.
patches.replace: Pasá, sentate.
patches.why: Llamadas are in midsummer; 'hace frío' is wrong.

patches.find: Come in, it’s cold.
patches.replace: Come in, sit down.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: desde Navidad, al dispensador
patches.replace: desde principios de diciembre, al dispensador
patches.why: Plot logic: on c.26 Dec a 'since Christmas' pattern of a pack every two days is impossible to notice, and Wilkin's 4 kg loss runs from early December.

patches.find: since Christmas, the napkin dispenser
patches.replace: since early December, the napkin dispenser
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: por primera vez en un mes, todavía
patches.replace: por primera vez en mes y medio, todavía
patches.why: Consistency with the napkin timeline (early Dec to 15 Jan).

patches.find: for the first time in a month
patches.replace: for the first time in six weeks
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: cada dos días desde Navidad?
patches.replace: cada dos días desde principios de diciembre?
patches.why: Quiz follows story fix.

patches.find: These formulas are frozen: the verb never changes (always sepa, digamos, sea).
patches.replace: Most of these formulas are frozen (always sepa, digamos, sea); ¡ni que…! lets you choose the verb, but keeps it in the past subjunctive.
patches.why: Accuracy: the card's own example (ni que estuviera) shows the verb in ni que does change.

patches.find: ¡Ni que…! always takes the imperfect subjunctive, even about the present.
patches.replace: ¡Ni que…! takes the past subjunctive (here the imperfect), even about the present.
patches.why: Accuracy: pluperfect subjunctive is also used after ni que.

patches.find: "say": "Wow. Then we fix the menu and the real problem.
patches.replace: "say": "OK. Then we fix the menu and, with tact, the real problem.
patches.why: After reply 2 ('habría que preguntárselo... sin pruebas') nothing has been revealed, so 'Wow' is a non sequitur.

patches.find: "en": "Wow. Then we fix the menu and the real problem.
patches.replace: "en": "OK. Then we fix the menu and, tactfully, the real problem.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: una obra que el pueblo canta en contra se la acaba comiendo el monte
patches.replace: una obra a la que el pueblo le canta en contra se la acaba comiendo el monte
patches.why: Relative clause lacked its preposition ('cantarle en contra a algo'); non-standard in narration.

patches.find: “I haven’t written it, dear. I swear
patches.replace: “I didn’t write it, dear. I swear
patches.why: EN: natural English uses the simple past here.

patches.find: In Spanish oral poetry these combine with assonant rhyme (corriendo / durmiendo).
patches.replace: In Spanish oral poetry these combine with rhyme (corriendo / durmiendo is a full rhyme; most coplas rhyme by assonance).
patches.why: Wrong claim: corriendo/durmiendo is consonant (full) rhyme, not assonant.

patches.find: or choosing the wrong one (*Los planos lo habían dibujado)
patches.replace: or, in standard Spanish, choosing the wrong one (*Los planos la habían dibujado)
patches.why: The card itself presents Andean invariable lo as legitimate, so starring 'Los planos lo' contradicts it.

patches.find: With a fronted direct object the copy is obligatory
patches.replace: With a fronted definite direct object the copy is obligatory
patches.why: Accuracy (focus fronting takes no clitic).

patches.find: Complete: «Los planos ___ habían dibujado
patches.replace: Complete in standard Spanish: «Los planos ___ habían dibujado
patches.why: Ambiguity: per the card, Andean invariable 'lo' is also acceptable.

patches.find: "options": ["lo", "la", "les", "los"]
patches.replace: "options": ["le", "la", "les", "los"]
patches.why: Removes second defensible answer (invariable lo).

patches.find: I haven't written it, dear.
patches.replace: I didn't write it, dear.
patches.why: EN naturalness (matches story EN).

patches.find: Ojalá sea falsa, y ya está.
patches.replace: Ojalá sea falsa, y listo.
patches.why: 'y ya está' is Peninsular; Salvadoran usage is 'y listo'/'y ya'.

patches.find: con un comentario lleno de faltas
patches.replace: con un comentario tan breve como temerario
patches.why: The quoted comment has no spelling mistakes; new wording also hints at the self-incriminating detail.

patches.find: with a comment full of spelling mistakes
patches.replace: with a comment as brief as it was reckless
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: las ollas de enseñar en fila, las fichas
patches.replace: las ollas de enseñar en fila, que a nadie se le había ocurrido contar, las fichas
patches.why: Plot hole: once they suspect a replica (Wed), why is the storeroom only checked on Friday? Acknowledge the oversight.

patches.find: the teaching pots in a row, the cards
patches.replace: the teaching pots in a row, which nobody had thought to count, the cards
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: and drove down to the site with Dayana at the wheel
patches.replace: and went down to the site with Dayana at the wheel
patches.why: EN: he does not drive; Dayana does.

patches.find: Yesenia thinks the hope is unlikely to come true.
patches.replace: Neftalí thinks the hope is unlikely to come true.
patches.why: Wrong attribution: «Ojalá fuera tan fácil, niña» is Neftalí's line.

patches.find: no lo dice ningún dato
patches.replace: no lo respalda ningún dato
patches.why: Collocation: data 'support' (respaldar) a claim; matches EN 'isn't backed by'.

c2-01.grade: A- : genuinely C2 (dry judicial irony, truncated refranes, mood-for-stance all natural and spread), excellent cabina clue; one age/timeline slip fixed
issues_fixed: Timeline: Fali (58) could not have heard a 1984 tape 'con nueve años' -> quince/instituto (+EN)
Logic: she goes down to the storeroom FOR the cassette box (box was in the trastero she was clearing)
Agreement: '—grabados de la radio—' with no masculine plural referent
EN 'the judge's children plagiarise' (Spanish twists 'casa', not children) in story + role-play
EN 'The theatre brought the house down' -> 'The house came down'
Card + gq: '¡ni que…! always/needs the imperfect subjunctive' (pluperfect subjunctive also standard)
Role-play: 'a la señoría' -> 'a su señoría'; Fali 'grabé ese ensayo' contradicts story (nephew posted it)
Goal opener 'tres días antes de tu actuación' contradicts the story (visit is the day before)
issues_open: 'El tercer cuplé' on the 1984 tape: COAC groups sing two cuplés per performance; a carnival expert may prefer 'el segundo'
Plausibility of a sitting judge on the COAC jury 15 years ago (writer flagged)
Cádiz speech items (ustedes os creéis, quilla to a 63-year-old, jartible, levantar un chiste) and verse metre for a carnival author
'no está nada mal' explained as 'strong approval' in the card: range is moderate-to-strong; acceptable

c2-02.grade: A : the strongest of the five; free indirect speech, ellipsis and Rioplatense dislocation are literary and natural; facts verified (3 Dec 1978 eviction, Cuareim 1080, Martínez Reina factory in Capurro, Ley 18.059)
issues_fixed: Timeline: 'llevaba doce días durmiendo mal' at the repair, 2-3 days after finding the crack -> tres noches (+EN)
'palillos' -> 'palos' (candombe is played with one palo)
Card: clitic 'obligatory' with any fronted object -> definite topic (focus fronting takes none)

Role-play: 'hace frío' in Montevideo's midsummer (dialogue + goal opener); learner switches vos/usted with don Obdulio; opener reply asked about a crack in a drum already repaired; gender-assuming 'amiga'
issues_open: Montevideo check: 'palos' vs 'palillos', caldera (kettle), chusma, saco in February, comparsa order
Current use of the Cuareim 1080 site ('cooperativa de viviendas') not re-verified; the Mediomundo surnames on the list should not match a prominent real family
Afro-Hispanic lexicon topic is thin on true loanwords (story uses Spanish-based candombe terms; card admits this): owner may accept

c2-03.grade: B+ : lively, well-clued and the code-switching is purposeful, but lighter C2 (more C1+ banter) and the napkin timeline had a hole; institutional realism needs an owner call
issues_fixed: Plot hole: napkin pattern 'desde Navidad' noticed c.26 Dec and inconsistent with a weight loss from early December -> 'desde principios de diciembre' + payoff 'mes y medio' + quiz q2 (+EN)
Card: 'the verb never changes' contradicted by its own ni que estuviera example
gq why: ni que 'always' imperfect subjunctive
Role-play closing 'Wow…' was a non sequitur after the cautious reply branch
issues_open: Realism: MLB rules limit unsigned prospects' stays at team academies (e.g. 15 days in any 45 near eligibility), yet Wilkin eats there for weeks among 'ochenta muchachos'; owner may reframe as a showcase/training camp or accept as fiction
A 14-year-old hired as kitchen hand: DR labour code allows 14+ with restrictions; consider 'de ayudante, por las tardes y con permiso de su mamá' or a teacher note
'no está nada mal, para una dieta que nunca ha visto un plátano' said of Courtney's dough is strained (works perfectly in the role-play about Plan B); keep or reword story + card + concepts together
The 'machine-translated' WhatsApp report reads as fluent Spanish, so the joke does not land; a calque or two would help
'Mind yuh business', '¿Qué lo que?', jevi, ponerse para su número, el sazón: eastern Dominican / cocolo speaker check
Guloya instruments: sources give flauta, tambora/bombo, redoblante, triángulo; 'tambores y pitos' acceptable

c2-04.grade: A- : real C2 (Andean evidentials, stance diminutives, oral-poetry rhetoric), superb double-meaning copla and literal-oath payoff; card errors fixed
issues_fixed: Relative clause 'una obra que el pueblo canta en contra' -> 'a la que el pueblo le canta en contra'
Card: corriendo/durmiendo called assonant rhyme (it is full rhyme)
Card starred '*Los planos lo habían dibujado' while presenting Andean invariable lo as legitimate; gq item then had two defensible answers (lo/los) -> stem 'in standard Spanish' and option lo -> le
EN 'I haven't written it' -> 'I didn't write it' (story + role-play)
issues_open: Surname Pinedo evokes the Afro-Bolivian royal house (Julio Pinedo, Mururata): owner may rename the foreman
Simona apparently did not know her grandfather lies in the old cemetery ('si no me equivoco'): fine as politeness, but a reader may query it
Jacinta's tú vs vos with Simona, invariable lo for an elder (respectful, not caricature?), saya details (who sings coplas, costumes): Tocaña community check
'Mazamorra' and 'progresiva' as Bolivian engineering usage: Bolivian engineer check

c2-05.grade: A- : strong C2 register contrast (rumour conditional, academic hedging, correction notice), facts accurate (Loma Caldera, 1976 silos, 1978 University of Colorado), chip clue planted in line 1; small plot hole patched
issues_fixed: Plot hole: storeroom only checked two days after they identify a replica -> 'que a nadie se le había ocurrido contar' (+EN)
'comentario lleno de faltas' while the quoted comment has none
Peninsular 'y ya está' in Salvadoran mouth -> 'y listo'
EN 'drove down' when Dayana drives
gq attributes «Ojalá fuera tan fácil» to Yesenia (it is Neftalí's line)
Role-play collocation 'no lo dice ningún dato' -> 'no lo respalda'
issues_open: The stolen replica, now police evidence, back in the workshop the following Thursday: plausible but quick
First photo shows the bird 'all the way round' yet hides the rim chip: lighting explains it; optional clarifying phrase
Invented 'completed tail' by a 1990s illustrator on a real museum's panel: owner may want a teacher note that it is fiction
Salvadoran lexicon (cipote, chivo, chumpa, tacuacín, jalar agua para su molino) and vos/usted asymmetry: native check
